      "species": [],

      "verbatim": "In culture models, neuroprotective efficacy was superior to the control condition in 74% of experimental results, and no different or inferior to the control condition in 23% and 3% of cases, respectively."

      "species": [],
      "n": null,

      "verbatim": "As the quality of evidence increased with more STAIR standards being met, the average level of neuroprotection of drugs tended to regress toward the overall mean of approximately 25%."

      "verbatim": "When drugs are tested more extensively in focal models of ischemia (maximum scope of testing \u2020 10), then the average level of neuroprotection tends not to differ greatly from the mean level of protection (25%)."

      "verbatim": "There was no evidence that drugs used clinically (114 drugs) were more effective experimentally than those tested only in animal models (912 drugs), for example, improvement in focal models averaged 31.3 \u2020 16.7% versus 24.4 \u2020 32.9%, p > 0.05, respectively."

  "headline_index": 0,
  "what_the_study_did": "The study compared the experimental efficacy and scope of testing of drugs used clinically for acute stroke with those tested only experimentally in animal models.",
  "what_it_found": "Drugs used clinically were not found to be more effective experimentally than those tested only in animal models, and the scope of testing was highly variable with no clear relationship between mechanism and efficacy.",
  "key_quotes": [
    {
      "quote": "There was no evidence that drugs used clinically (114 drugs) were more effective experimentally than those tested only in animal models (912 drugs), for example, improvement in focal models averaged 31.3 \u2020 16.7% versus 24.4 \u2020 32.9%, p > 0.05, respectively.",
      "topic": "Clinical vs Experimental Efficacy"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Scope of testing using Stroke Therapy Academic Industry Roundtable (STAIR) criteria was highly variable, and no relationship was found between mechanism and efficacy.",
      "topic": "Scope of Testing"
    },
    {
      "quote": "The results question whether the most efficacious drugs are being selected for stroke clinical trials.",
      "topic": "Drug Selection"
    },
    {
      "quote": "A common perception of neuroprotection research is that everything works in animals but nothing works in people.",
      "topic": "Animal vs Human Results"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Those drugs given to acute stroke patients were not distinguished by superior efficacy in animal models of focal ischemia compared with all drugs that have been tested only experimentally.",
      "topic": "Efficacy Comparison"
    },
    {
      "quote": "An intervention should be considered for clinical trial only when there is both a high level of experimental efficacy and a diverse body of evidence supporting its clinical application.",
      "topic": "Clinical Trial Criteria"
    }
  ]
